tagline: Gear that looks like it works.
sector: E-commerce and retail, value-band recovery and overlanding gear
founded_place_size: Founded 2019 in Boulder, Colorado. Small owner-run shop, under ten people, selling on a marketplace and its own storefront.
about: We make recovery straps, soft shackles and overlanding kit for people with a lifted truck and a real budget. Nine SKUs from 35 to 220 dollars. Our buyer is not paying for a name, he is paying because the gear looks like it will hold when he is stuck at dusk on a fire road. The detail is the whole argument: the stitching and the hardware finish are what separate us from the cheap import sitting next to us in search results.
audience: Off-road and 4x4 owners aged 25 to 50, buying on rugged credibility and price. They trust flat daylight and visible workmanship and they distrust anything that looks staged or expensive.
price_positioning: Value band, 35 to 220 dollars. The look is bright, hard-wearing and legible, honest daylight on the plain-ground shots and unstyled dust on the field shots. Never premium-expedition cinematic, never discount-banner loud. Either extreme reads as pretending and loses the buyer.
typography: Type should read as workwear signage: a sturdy condensed or grotesque for headlines and spec callouts, a clean neutral text face for body and the range table. Bold but balanced, plenty of negative space, nothing magazine-like.
voice: Blunt and plain. We say what the gear does and what it is rated for. Certified working loads are stated as certified and never rounded or dressed up.
brand_assets_status: The only brand mark file we can find is a flat screen-size export our old developer left us, plus a photo of the same mark on a woven label. We have no scalable artwork and no written guidelines. Charcoal is our storefront ground and Ridge Blue is the new webbing colour we are introducing. Treat the notes above as direction, not a locked system.
values: Honesty in the picture and the spec. Durability over shine. Fair price for real capability. If an edit would make the product look like something it is not, we would rather it stayed plain.
